evidence.title: Build the foundation for
evidence.copy: Reliable team analysis depends on tracking the game across time. CourtFlux focuses first on player movement, team classification and ball continuity so later possessions, events and tactical structure can be built on stronger evidence rather than guessed from isolated frames.
evidence.note: Shared staff collaboration, advanced player identity and richer structured team analytics will continue to mature with the product; they should not be interpreted as fully finished beta capabilities today.

faq.question: Who is the Team workflow aimed at?
faq.answer: It is aimed at the staff around one basketball team: coaches, assistants and performance or video analysts who want a repeatable analysis workflow around the same game history.

faq.question: Does every staff member need to prepare a roster before analysis?
faq.answer: No. The first analysis only requires home and away teams. Roster and jersey information is optional and can be added when player-level identity becomes useful.

faq.question: Can staff return to older analyses?
faq.answer: Yes. My Analyses provides a searchable and filterable history of the workspace's analysis runs, including processing state and saved results.

faq.question: What happens to uploaded source video?
faq.answer: Direct uploads are scheduled for deletion 60 days after upload. Analysis results and statistics remain available after the source video is removed.

faq.question: Does CourtFlux already provide tactical recommendations?
faq.answer: No. Tactical intelligence remains part of the longer-term product direction. Current customer-facing beta results stay focused on validated player, team and ball tracking evidence.
